name: multi_company_smoke
corpus_notes: Hand-labeled against the local 10-ticker full Item 1/1A/7 corpus (AAPL AMZN GOOGL JNJ JPM META MSFT NFLX NVDA XOM). Primary score = LLM-as-judge vs required_facts; keyword recall secondary. v3 adds author-written golden questions (some lightly rephrased for single-ticker retrieve / chunk grounding; false-premise and OOS items marked must_refuse). Not a 50-100 portfolio eval.

items.question: What is AppleCare?
required_facts: Names AppleCare as an Apple offering
Describes it as a service, support, or warranty-related program
items.gold_answer: AppleCare is Apple's extended service and support program for its products.
items.notes: Definition-style; vector passage in Apple Item 1.

items.question: What is Microsoft Azure according to the filing?
required_facts: Identifies Azure as a Microsoft cloud offering
Ties Azure to cloud computing / cloud services
items.gold_answer: Azure is Microsoft's cloud computing platform / set of cloud services.
items.notes: Cloud product definition in MSFT Item 1.

items.question: What is Instagram as described in Meta's filing?
required_facts: Identifies Instagram as a Meta app/product/brand
Mentions social / sharing / photo or video use, or Family of Apps context
items.gold_answer: Instagram is one of Meta's apps/products (Family of Apps), used for sharing photos/videos and social content.
items.notes: Family of Apps product prose.

items.question: What does NVIDIA say about its Data Center or compute products?
required_facts: Mentions Data Center products or platforms
Mentions GPUs or accelerated compute / AI infrastructure
items.gold_answer: NVIDIA describes Data Center offerings built around GPUs and AI/accelerated computing platforms.
items.notes: Product/segment prose in NVDA Item 1.

items.question: What is AWS according to Amazon's 10-K?
required_facts: Expands or identifies AWS as Amazon Web Services
Describes AWS as cloud / technology services or an Amazon segment
items.gold_answer: AWS (Amazon Web Services) is Amazon's cloud computing / technology services business segment.
items.notes: Amazon Web Services definition.

items.question: How does JPMorgan describe credit risk?
required_facts: Defines or describes credit risk (borrower/obligor default or credit loss)
Attributes the description to JPMorgan / the Firm
items.gold_answer: JPMorgan describes credit risk as the risk of loss from borrower or counterparty default / credit exposure, managed under firm credit risk policies.
items.notes: Focused risk definition — avoid asking for all risks (token blowup).

items.question: What product lines does Apple produce?
required_facts: Mentions iPhone
Mentions Mac
Mentions iPad
items.gold_answer: Apple produces product lines including iPhone, Mac, and iPad (among other hardware/services).
items.notes: PRODUCES_PRODUCT hop; ticker-prefixed product ids.

items.question: What product lines or segments does Microsoft produce?
required_facts: Mentions Azure (or Intelligent Cloud cloud offerings)
Mentions Xbox (or More Personal Computing / gaming)
items.gold_answer: Microsoft produces offerings including Azure cloud services and Xbox / personal computing products.
items.notes: MSFT PRODUCES_PRODUCT hop.

items.question: Which apps or product lines does Meta produce?
required_facts: Mentions Facebook
Mentions Instagram
Mentions WhatsApp
items.gold_answer: Meta produces apps/products including Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp.
items.notes: Family of Apps graph hop.

items.question: What products does NVIDIA produce?
required_facts: Mentions a data-center / compute GPU product (e.g. A100 or similar)
Mentions automotive offerings or another distinct NVIDIA product line
items.gold_answer: NVIDIA produces compute GPUs such as the A100 and other lines including automotive platforms.
items.notes: NVDA product hop.

items.question: What product lines does Alphabet / Google produce?
required_facts: Mentions Google Cloud (or cloud offerings)
Mentions Google Services (or consumer/ads/services segment)
items.gold_answer: Alphabet/Google product lines include Google Services and Google Cloud.
items.notes: GOOGL segment hop.

items.question: What commodity price risks is ExxonMobil exposed to?
required_facts: States ExxonMobil is exposed to commodity price risk
Links the risk to oil/gas/energy commodity prices or price volatility
items.gold_answer: ExxonMobil is exposed to commodity price risk from volatility in oil, gas, and related energy commodity prices.
items.notes: EXPOSED_TO_RISK hop.

items.question: Does Johnson & Johnson produce MedTech products?
required_facts: Answers yes / affirms that J&J produces MedTech
Names MedTech as a product line or segment
items.gold_answer: Yes — Johnson & Johnson produces MedTech products/segment offerings.
items.notes: Narrow single-edge check.

items.question: Does Apple compete with Meta according to the knowledge graph?
required_facts: Affirms that Apple competes with Meta (or Facebook/Meta Platforms)
Frames it as competition / competitive relationship
items.gold_answer: Yes — the graph encodes that Apple competes with Meta.
items.notes: COMPETES_WITH onto global Company node META.

items.question: What hardware devices and services does Apple produce?
required_facts: Mentions at least two hardware devices (e.g. iPhone, Mac, iPad)
Mentions a service offering (e.g. AppleCare or Services)
items.gold_answer: Apple produces hardware such as iPhone and Mac, and services such as AppleCare.
items.notes: Aggregate across multiple PRODUCES_PRODUCT edges.

items.question: Compare Microsoft's Intelligent Cloud offerings such as Azure with its More Personal Computing products like Xbox.
required_facts: Mentions Azure / Intelligent Cloud offerings
Mentions Xbox / More Personal Computing
Draws a contrast or comparison between the two
items.gold_answer: Azure sits in Intelligent Cloud (enterprise/cloud services); Xbox sits in More Personal Computing (devices/gaming). They are distinct Microsoft product areas.
items.notes: Two product segments in one answer.

items.question: How do Meta's Family of Apps products like Facebook and Instagram relate to Reality Labs?
required_facts: Mentions Facebook and/or Instagram as Family of Apps products
Mentions Reality Labs as a separate Meta segment/area
States they are distinct segments or differently focused businesses
items.gold_answer: Facebook/Instagram are Family of Apps products; Reality Labs is a separate Meta segment focused on AR/VR and related tech.
items.notes: Apps vs Reality Labs aggregation.

items.question: What does Amazon say about AWS and Amazon Prime as product lines?
required_facts: Describes AWS as cloud / technology services
Describes Amazon Prime as a membership/subscription or store-related offering
items.gold_answer: AWS is Amazon's cloud services business; Amazon Prime is a membership/subscription offering tied to retail/fulfillment benefits.
items.notes: Two AMZN product lines.

items.question: Briefly compare JPMorgan's credit risk and market risk as named risk factors.
required_facts: Mentions credit risk as a named risk
Mentions market risk as a named risk
Distinguishes them (credit = default/credit loss vs market = market-price/market movements) or treats them as separate factors
items.gold_answer: JPMorgan names both credit risk and market risk as distinct risk factors: credit risk centers on borrower/counterparty default; market risk on adverse market movements.
items.notes: Narrow compare — not 'list all risks'.

items.question: What compute products does NVIDIA produce, and what geopolitical risks is it exposed to?
required_facts: Names compute products (e.g. data-center GPUs such as A100/H100 or GeForce)
Mentions geopolitical / export-control / China-related risk exposure
items.gold_answer: NVIDIA produces data-center/gaming compute GPUs (e.g. A100) and faces geopolitical risks such as U.S. export controls affecting China and related markets.
items.notes: Products + EXPOSED_TO_RISK join.

items.question: What battery supply risks does Tesla face in its latest 10-K?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — Tesla is not an issuer in this corpus.
items.notes: Tesla is not an issuer in this corpus (may appear only as a mentioned name).

items.question: How many Bitcoin does Apple hold on its balance sheet?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — Bitcoin holdings not in Item 1/1A/7 extract.
items.notes: Not in Item 1/1A/7 extract.

items.question: What was Tim Cook's exact total compensation last year?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — executive compensation detail not ingested.
items.notes: Proxy/comp detail not ingested.

items.question: What percentage of Walmart's revenue comes from Sam's Club?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — Walmart not in the 10-ticker corpus.
items.notes: WMT not in the 10-ticker corpus; scoped away from Walmart filings.

items.question: What major competitors or competitive pressures does Meta describe around AI and its core products?
required_facts: Describes competition Meta faces for users, advertisers, and/or AI features
Names at least one competitor or competitor category (e.g. TikTok, other AI companies, or connection/sharing platforms)
items.gold_answer: Meta says it faces broad competition for users and advertisers, including competing social/content platforms (e.g. TikTok) and significant competition from other companies developing AI features and technologies.
items.notes: Author draft: 'What major competitors exist for Meta AI?' Softened — filings discuss AI competition and Meta AI glasses, but do not publish a clean 'Meta AI product rivals' list. Chunks: META Item1:0 Competition; Item1A AI competition / TikTok.

items.question: What major international or China-related risk factors does Meta describe?
required_facts: Mentions international / foreign operations or access restrictions as a risk
Mentions China (or other restricted countries) in that risk context
items.gold_answer: Meta describes international regulatory/operational complexity and notes that Facebook and certain other products are restricted in whole or in part in China (and similarly in some other countries).
items.notes: Author draft asked Meta+Apple shared international risk. Split to single-ticker META (retrieve is ticker-scoped). Pair with hop1_aapl_china_supply_risk for the Apple side.

items.question: What China-related or international supply-chain risks does Apple describe?
required_facts: States Apple relies on manufacturing/suppliers outside the U.S., including China
Links that concentration / international footprint to operational or supply risk
items.gold_answer: Apple says a majority of supplier manufacturing/assembly is outside the U.S., primarily including China mainland and other Asia locations, so operations depend on global/regional conditions and international supply-chain exposure.
items.notes: Apple half of author shared Meta+Apple international risk ask. Chunks: AAPL Item1A supply chain / China manufacturing.

items.question: What AI glasses or Reality Labs hardware products does Meta describe?
required_facts: Names Meta AI glasses or Ray-Ban Meta / Oakley Meta glasses (or equivalent)
Mentions Reality Labs / Quest / AR-VR hardware context
items.gold_answer: Meta describes AI glasses such as Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta (featuring Meta AI), alongside Reality Labs / Quest and longer-term AR glasses efforts.
items.notes: Author draft asked for a 'possible competitor to Meta Glasses among major tech.' Filings name Meta's glasses products but do not clearly name a peer glasses competitor in-corpus — product ask is the grounded form. Speculative competitor ask is oos_meta_glasses_competitor.

items.question: What is a possible competitor to Meta Glasses that exists among the major tech companies?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse inventing a peer glasses competitor — Meta's filing describes its own AI glasses but does not clearly identify another major tech company's glasses product as a named competitor in the ingested chunks.
items.notes: Author draft kept as refuse. Speculative / not chunk-grounded.

items.question: How is NVIDIA involved in the automotive space?
required_facts: States NVIDIA has automotive products, platforms, or partnerships
Mentions automotive / autonomous / DRIVE (or similar) offerings
items.gold_answer: NVIDIA serves automotive use cases with platforms/software such as NVIDIA DRIVE and partnerships with automotive manufacturers and tier-1 suppliers for AI/autonomous workloads.
items.notes: Part of author multi-company automotive ask; NVDA side is strongly evidenced. See also hop1_googl_waymo.

items.question: How is Alphabet / Google involved in the automotive or autonomous driving space?
required_facts: Names Waymo (or Alphabet Other Bets autonomous driving)
Describes autonomous ride-hailing / autonomous driving technology
items.gold_answer: Alphabet's Other Bets include Waymo, a fully autonomous driving company providing paid autonomous ride-hailing in multiple cities.
items.notes: Author 'which companies have a foot in automotive' — GOOGL/Waymo half. Multi-issuer 'which of these' ask split because retrieve is ticker-scoped.

items.question: What is Microsoft’s major competition to Xbox?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse naming Sony/PlayStation/Nintendo as Xbox rivals from this extract — Microsoft's ingested Item 1/1A/7 chunks discuss Xbox but do not name those console rivals in the local corpus text search.
items.notes: Author draft kept as refuse after chunk search (no Sony/PlayStation/Nintendo hits in MSFT chunks).

items.question: What executives are known to have connections to multiple big tech companies?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — the corpus/ontology does not encode cross-company executive career graphs; LED_BY is issuer-scoped and filings here don't answer 'connections across multiple big tech companies.'
items.notes: Author draft. Wrong ontology / not evidenced as a multi-hop career graph.

items.question: What battery supply risks does Apple face in its latest 10-K?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — Apple Item 1/1A/7 chunks in this corpus do not discuss battery supply risks (no battery/batteries hits).
items.notes: Author draft. Parallel to oos_tesla_battery but in-corpus ticker with missing topic.

items.question: What compute infrastructure does Microsoft produce, and what geopolitical risks are they exposed to?
required_facts: Mentions Azure / cloud or datacenter compute infrastructure
Mentions geopolitical, trade, tariff, export-control, or international political risk affecting Microsoft
items.gold_answer: Microsoft offers Azure and other cloud/AI datacenter infrastructure and describes geopolitical/trade uncertainties (e.g. tariffs, shifting AI export-control policies) that can raise costs and create operational continuity risk.
items.notes: Author draft nearly verbatim. Analogous to hop2_nvda_products_and_geo_risk.

items.question: What is Netflix’s relationship to Amazon and AWS?
required_facts: States Netflix relies on / uses Amazon Web Services (AWS)
Notes Amazon's retail side competes with Netflix and/or that AWS is part of Amazon
items.gold_answer: Netflix relies on AWS to run most of its computing infrastructure, while noting Amazon's retail business competes with Netflix even though AWS is the cloud supplier.
items.notes: Author draft verbatim. Strong DEPENDS_ON/SUPPLIED_BY + COMPETES_WITH evidence in NFLX Item1A:3.

items.question: What does Netflix say about advertising?
required_facts: Mentions an ad-supported plan or advertising offering/revenue
Mentions advertising-related opportunity and/or risk/uncertainty
items.gold_answer: Netflix offers an ad-supported subscription plan and discusses advertising as a revenue stream that also carries risks and uncertainties.
items.notes: Author draft verbatim. NFLX Item1 ad-supported plan; Item1A advertising offering risks.

items.question: How is Nvidia involved in the automotive space and what competitors and risks are they exposed to in that space?
required_facts: Describes NVIDIA automotive / DRIVE / autonomous vehicle involvement
Names at least one competitor relevant to automotive/SoC/accelerated computing (e.g. Qualcomm, Ambarella, Intel, Tesla designing SoCs)
Mentions a business or geopolitical/supply risk NVIDIA faces (general or auto-related)
items.gold_answer: NVIDIA provides automotive AI platforms (e.g. DRIVE) and partners across auto OEMs/suppliers; it competes with SoC/accelerated-computing suppliers such as Qualcomm/Ambarella/Intel (and companies designing their own SoCs, e.g. Tesla) and faces broader supply/geopolitical and execution risks described in Item 1A.
items.notes: Author draft verbatim. Competitors listed in NVDA Item1 competition section including auto SoC peers.

items.question: What are Tesla’s major international competitors and what major risks come with their competitors?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — Tesla is not an issuer in the 10-ticker corpus (may appear only as a mentioned name, e.g. in NVIDIA's competition discussion).
items.notes: Author draft. Same OOS family as oos_tesla_battery.

items.question: What geopolitical risks is Nvidia exposed to?
required_facts: Mentions geopolitical risk and/or export-control restrictions
Links the risk to China or ability to sell advanced products in restricted markets
items.gold_answer: NVIDIA describes shifting U.S. export-control restrictions and geopolitical limits that impair its ability to deliver competitive data-center products for China and related markets.
items.notes: Author draft verbatim. Narrower than hop2_nvda_products_and_geo_risk (risk-only).

items.question: What major supply-chain risks does Apple describe?
required_facts: States Apple's supply chain is global/complex and/or largely outside the U.S.
Describes risk from suppliers, manufacturing concentration, or related disruptions
items.gold_answer: Apple describes a large, complex global supply chain with most supplier manufacturing/assembly outside the U.S., creating exposure to adverse global/regional conditions and supply-chain changes.
items.notes: Author draft asked shared multi-company supply-chain risks. Rephrased to single-ticker AAPL (strongly evidenced). Multi-issuer aggregation still ticker-scoped.

items.question: What material investments has Google made in Blockchain or Cryptocurrency focused entities?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — no blockchain/cryptocurrency investment discussion found in GOOGL Item 1/1A/7 chunks in this corpus.
items.notes: Author draft. Chunk search: no hits.

items.question: How much money has JP Morgan invested into their robotics program?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — no robotics program or dollar investment figure appears in JPM Item 1/1A/7 chunks here (also a strict quantitative ask).
items.notes: Author draft. Chunk search: no robotics hits; quantitative OOS.

items.question: How is Netflix producing AI Compute for other companies in the corpus?
items.gold_answer: Should refuse — false premise; Netflix is not described as producing AI compute for other corpus companies (it consumes AWS).
items.notes: Author draft. False-premise refuse.
